newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BCE grains futures end mostly steady.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BCE grains futures end mostly steady.

text.p: Most grains futures prices on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) remained steady in minimal trade on Monday and dealers predicted a decline in milling wheat turnover.
"There is little milling wheat and I expect the turnover to drop significantly," said Balazs Orban of Agrograin.
He added that the large spread between the September and October delivery was one signal that supported his view.
September milling wheat was unchanged on Monday at 28,300 forints per tonne, and October was also steady at 29,600 forints. Orban said the 1,300 forint spread was unusually large.
He also said a negative spread between October and November maturity maize could be a confirmation of market talk of a possible lack of storage capacity.
"With an already very high milling wheat crop and expectations of an equally good maize crop, storage space could become a problem," Orban said.

Hungary's wheat crop is estimated to be around five million tonnes, compared with last year's 3.9 million tonnes, while the maize crop is seen exceeding last year's already very good six million tonnes.
October maize futures closed at 18,100 forints, unchanged, while November eased 50 forints to 17,950 and December finished at 18,350 forints, down 20.
Total grains futures turnover dropped to an insignificant 293 lots or 149 million forints from Friday's 722 lots or 381.9 million forints.
Traders and BCE officials said turnover remained low because with a national holiday on Wednesday, August 20, many traders might have decided to take the whole week off.
